topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address conventional treatment modalities and the challenges of non-specific systemic toxicity and drug efflux mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular and genetic vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit tumor-specific biological dependencies, checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore kinase oncogene addiction along with the molecular design, limitations, and resistance pathways associated with small-molecule kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the therapeutic application of unconjugated monoclonal antibodies and toxin-linked antibody conjugates to target tumor surface markers.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and T-cell immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for natural anti-tumor immunity and therapeutic strategies designed to re-engage or engineer T cells against cancer.

topics.label: Therapeutic progress, ongoing challenges, and future paradigms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical clinical gains, current management limitations, and emerging paradigms shaping the future of cancer care.
